source.title: The Orthogonality of Weight Vectors: The Key Characteristics of Normalization and Residual Connections
source.authors: Zhi-Xing Lu; Yuan-Yuan Sun; Zhi-Hao Yang; Qinghua Zhou; Hongfei Lin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equation and table formatting is flattened, but relevant main tables remain legible.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether adding normalization and residual connections changes weight-vector orthogonality and reports resulting PII values and test accuracy. It does not measure training classification error, so its evidence is a related optimization/performance measure rather than the claim's stated outcome.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper’s own PII and test-accuracy comparisons for normalization plus residual connections, and the optimizer PII comparison. No training-error result is reported. Values cited from prior work and figure-only displays without a recoverable condition-to-value mapping are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures weight-vector orthogonality, its preservation by optimizers, and final test accuracy. These do not test training error, depth-related training degradation, initialization-dependent training speed, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization speed. Its theoretical argument concerns orthogonality rather than a specific qualification or refutation of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that normalization combined with residual connections improves or preserves weight-vector orthogonality, promotes diagonal dominance of the weight Gram matrix, and thereby improves feature learning and performance. They also conclude that LoRA preserves orthogonality. Their reported empirical outcomes are PII and final test accuracy, not direct measurements of the training outcomes in V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates PII and test accuracy under controlled optimizer and normalization/residual conditions; it does not use the claim versions’ training-error recipes. It reports network experiments and measurements of pretrained-model parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: PII changes with optimizer; the paper reports SGD has better conformal capability than Adam, AdamW and RMSprop. PII is also reported under different activations and with or without normalization plus residual connections.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD preserves initial PII more closely than Adam in the reported FNN and CNN layers; the authors also report higher test accuracy with momentum-based optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizers differ in how strongly they preserve angles between weight vectors during training; angle preservation need not imply higher final test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly adding normalization and residual connections lowers PII and raises final test accuracy in the reported FNN and CNN comparisons. Table 4's CNN values are recoverable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested architectures and recipes, normalization combined with residual connections improves weight-vector orthogonality and final test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer and pretrained-model weight matrices have low PII; the custom Transformer's final fully connected matrix, which omits the combination, has PII 0.162.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-vector orthogonality is common in the measured Transformer-based models; the custom Transformer shows an association between layer configuration and PII.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 reports low Qwen PII before and after LoRA fine-tuning, with some matrix-specific increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested Qwen fine-tuning experiment, LoRA retains broadly low weight-vector PII.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-24), 2024
record.problems: The paper does not report training classification error or training speed. Several network results are presented as PII and test-accuracy comparisons rather than direct tests of the claim versions. Table 4 is flattened in the supplied text so its condition-to-value mapping cannot be reliably reconstructed. The FNN/CNN table entries do not identify a particular dataset in the table text, though the experiments are described as using MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 contains additional PII values for T5/Decoder and LLMs, including Qwen before and after LoRA fine-tuning. They are not included because the table’s flattened layout does not reliably support assigning every PII value to each subject and parameter-matrix column. This leaves the Transformer, PLM and LLM measurements incomplete; see Section 4.3, Table 5. Table 4 values are also omitted where row-to-condition mapping cannot be recovered; see Section 4.3, Table 4.

untested.parts: All parts: near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, model size, and training or regularization conditions.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
All parts: training error across depths, longer training, identity shortcuts preventing degradation, and the special-initialization exceptions.

All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. Post-training PII does not test these outcomes.
All parts: stability thresholds, transient loss rises, curvature changes, recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
All parts: speed of accuracy gain, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons. Final accuracy with normalization and residual connections jointly added does not test these outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V3, V4, and V6 verdicts: related measures and untested outcomes do not justify supports or limits_scope. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied versions, not because every numerical value is unreadable. R23–R26 belong to CNN Table 4; R27–R28 are redundant placeholders. Additional Table 5 measurements are declared in rows_left_out and do not bear on any supplied version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training duration are not tested.
Teacher-student spurious minima and width comparisons are not tested.

Training error across depth and identity shortcuts is not measured; the paper tests normalization plus residual connections on parameter orthogonality and test accuracy, not whether shortcuts prevent depth-related training degradation.
Activation-matched initialization and trainable depth are not compared. The paper compares optimizers’ effect on PII and tests whether normalization plus residual connections alter PII.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss increases, curvature, sharpness, and divergence are not measured.

Training speed, accuracy gain over training time, and learning-rate tolerance are not measured. The paper compares test accuracy and PII with versus without normalization and residual connections, and does not test Fixup.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports lower PII and higher test accuracy with normalization plus residual connections for the listed FNN activation and optimizer settings (R13-R26). These are orthogonality and test-accuracy results, not a direct training-error test.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported metric is final test accuracy rather than faster accuracy gain over time or tolerance to higher learning rates, so the study only partially addresses the version (R14,R16,R18,R20,R22,R24,R26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Optimizer comparisons in the FNN and CNN experiments
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that SGD keeps PII closer to its initial value than momentum optimizers in its comparisons, while the tested measure concerns conformal capability rather than activation-matched initialization or trainable depth (R1-R12).
